title: Isolation and Characterization of Human Bone Marrow Stromal Cells
author: Dzubanova, Ferencakova, et al.

steps.title: Dilute bone marrow and set gradient
steps.instruction: Dilute the bone marrow aspirate 1:1 in PBS containing CaCl₂ and MgCl₂, mix gently, and split the diluted aspirate equally into two 50 mL Falcon tubes.

steps.title: Layer Lymphoprep and centrifuge
steps.instruction: Using two small disposable needles, aspirate 10 mL of Lymphoprep, replace each needle with a Kwik‑plastic needle, place the needle at the bottom of each BM‑filled tube and gently add 10 mL Lymphoprep; centrifuge at 2 500 rpm (573 g) for 25 min at 20‑23 °C without brakes.

steps.title: Collect mononuclear layer and optional BMAT
steps.instruction: Prepare a 50 mL Falcon tube with 20 mL pre‑heated hBMSC isolation media. Using a glass Pasteur pipette with rubber teats, aspirate the narrow turbid middle phase (between Lymphoprep and the mononuclear cell layer) from each tube and transfer to the prepared tube; if a red clot is present, harvest it together with the turbid phase. Optionally, before collecting the middle phase, harvest the floating bone‑marrow adipose tissue (BMAT) layer on top, cutting the pipette tip if needed, wash BMAT with PBS, aliquot for RNA (add Trizol) or protein (add lysis buffer) and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Wash cells, count, and seed initial culture
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube containing the collected middle phase at 2 000 rpm (367 g) for 10 min at 20‑23 °C, aspirate the clear supernatant, resuspend the pellet in fresh hBMSC isolation media (≈10‑20 mL), count cells with 0.4 % trypan blue (1:1 dilution), and seed 10 × 10⁶ cells per T‑75 flask in 10 mL isolation media; incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ and do not change media for 7 days.

steps.title: Initial incubation without media change
steps.instruction: Maintain the seeded flasks for 7 days without changing the isolation media to allow hBMSCs to adhere to the plastic.

steps.title: Media changes and monitor confluence
steps.instruction: After 7 days, aspirate the isolation media and add fresh hBMSC cultivation media; thereafter change media every 2–3 days. When cells reach ~80 % confluence, either expand to the next passage or proceed to downstream assays. Do not keep cells in passage 0 for more than 1 month; otherwise passage to p1 or freeze.

steps.title: Passage or freeze cells
steps.instruction: For passaging: (a) aspirate culture media, (b) wash cells with 5–7 mL sterile PBS and incubate 5 min at 37 °C, (c) aspirate PBS, (d) add pre‑warmed Trypsin/EDTA (3 mL for T‑75, 5 mL for T‑150) and incubate 5 min at 37 °C, (e) add an equal volume of pre‑warmed complete hBMSC cultivation media to stop digestion, (f) gently resuspend cells, transfer to a 50 mL Falcon tube, (g) centrifuge at 1 200 rpm (132 g) for 5 min at 20‑23 °C, (h) resuspend pellet in appropriate volume of pre‑warmed media and count cells. For freezing: (i) after counting, prepare freezing media containing 1 × 10⁶ cells per 1 mL freezing media per CryoTube, (ii) centrifuge cell suspension at 1 200 rpm (132 g) for 5 min at 20‑23 °C, (iii) resuspend pellet in freezing media, (iv) store CryoTubes at –80 °C for 24 h then transfer to liquid nitrogen for long‑term storage. Avoid repeated freeze‑thaw cycles.

substeps.instruction: Wash with 5–7 mL PBS, incubate 5 min at 37 °C.
Add pre‑warmed Trypsin/EDTA (3 mL for T‑75, 5 mL for T‑150).
Add equal volume pre‑warmed complete media to stop digestion.
Resuspend and transfer to 50 mL tube.
Prepare freezing media (1 × 10⁶ cells per 1 mL).
Resuspend in freezing media, aliquot to CryoTubes.

steps.title: Seed cells for Seahorse assay
steps.instruction: Mark background wells on the XF24 cell culture microplate (wells 1A, 3B, 2C, 6D). Seed the remaining wells with 20 000 cells per well in 100 µL hBMSC culture media (3‑5 replicates per condition). After ≈3 h, add an additional 150 µL media to each well.

substeps.instruction: Incubate ~3 h, then add 150 µL media.

steps.title: Seed cells for ROS measurement
steps.instruction: Seed cells into a sterile black 96‑well plate with clear flat bottom at 15 000 cells per well in 200 µL culture media (5‑6 replicates per condition) and include at least two positive‑control wells treated with TBHP (cells, no test compounds).

steps.title: Seed cells for senescence assays
steps.instruction: For general senescence measurement, seed 10 000 cells per well in 200 µL culture media in a clear 96‑well plate (5‑6 replicates per condition). For β‑Galactosidase staining, seed 15 000 cells per well in 200 µL media in a clear 96‑well plate. Ensure consistent passage number across experiments; optionally coat plates (e.g., poly‑K, Cell‑Tak) if cells tend to detach.

substeps.instruction: Seed 10 000 cells/well (200 µL) for senescence assays.
Seed 15 000 cells/well (200 µL) for β‑Gal staining.
Optional: coat plates to improve attachment.

steps.title: Perform β‑Galactosidase staining
steps.instruction: Remove media and wash cells with 100 µL PBS per well. Add 100 µL 1× Fixative solution, incubate 15 min at room temperature, discard fixative and wash twice with 100 µL PBS (plates may be stored in PBS at 4 °C). Add 100 µL β‑Galactosidase Staining Solution, seal with parafilm, and incubate in a humidified 37 °C incubator without CO₂, avoiding evaporation. Begin imaging with an inverted microscope at 20× magnification between 6 and 12 h post‑incubation, checking every hour; extended incubation may cause over‑staining. For long‑term storage, replace staining solution with 70 % glycerol and store at 4 °C.

substeps.instruction: Discard fixative, wash twice with 100 µL PBS (optional storage at 4 °C).
Seal with parafilm, incubate 37 °C, no CO₂, humidified.
Image at 20× from 6‑12 h, hourly checks.
Optional: replace staining solution with 70 % glycerol, store 4 °C.

steps.title: Analyze SA‑β‑Gal data
steps.instruction: Save fluorescence intensity (SA‑β‑Gal activity) and protein absorbance (BCA assay) values in Excel. Calculate the ratio of fluorescence to absorbance for each well, compute the average ratio per treatment group, convert each ratio to a percentage of SA‑β‑Gal production, determine the average percentage per group, and plot the final percentages to compare treatments.

description: Bone marrow stromal cells (BMSCs) are a source of multipotent stem cells, which play an important role in the regulation of bone homeostasis and energy metabolism and represent a key source for tissue engineering, regenerative medicine, and diagnosis of metabolic and bone diseases. Previous studies, including our findings,1,2,3,4,5,6 demonstrated that the measurement of cellular metabolism including bioenergetics, production of reactive oxygen species (ROS), and senescence, among others is a critical feature to evaluate the stem cell potency and functional capacity of BMSCs in bone metabolism and regenerative processes in connection to different physiological and pathophysiological conditions. In the main manuscript connected to this STAR protocol,1 we reported that obesity causes hyperactivation of the metabolic status of human BMSCs (hBMSCs), characterized by upregulation of insulin signaling associated with enhanced mitochondrial respiration and ROS production, contributing to a senescent phenotype of hBMSCs. Thus, targeting cellular metabolism in metabolic and bone diseases has increased interest among researchers to develop new therapeutic approaches to regulate BMSC metabolism. Even though cellular metabolism can reflect the changes in cell proliferation, differentiation potential, cell survival, or inflammatory status, several advanced techniques can be applied to measure metabolic status of the cells. However, working with clinical material can limit how many different methods you can use to evaluate stem cell metabolism. Here, we present a step-by-step protocol for hBMSC isolation and characterization of hBMSC cellular metabolism, which we optimized for the measurement of bioenergetic profile, ROS production, and senescence, including tips for successfully setting up the protocol and troubleshooting of specific methods.
